# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✌ 👋 👊 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✌ 👋 👊 👆 👆 👆 👆 🤌 🫵 🙏]

My thinking: I'm Deaf — I see the bomb but I never hear a word anyone says. So the state I see is my only currency, and speech is how I spend it: my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. The crucial asymmetry: anything anyone wants to tell *me* must arrive as gesture.

Mute opened with a 21-sign sequence to me: 🤝, then ✌👋👦, then seven 👆, then ✌👋👦 again, then four 👆, then 🤌🫵🙏. Mute went first with zero information about the bomb, so this cannot be a bomb-specific instruction — it must be protocol bootstrap or a query. The cleanest parse: runs of 👆 as numbers, giving 7 then 4, with ✌👋👦 as some unit, 🤝 as greeting, and 🤌🫵🙏 as "you, please respond." I'll echo back 7 and 4 in my own proposed number code to confirm I parsed it, and — since Mute can hear — I'll define a full gesture code out loud so Mute can query me reliably from now on. Most importantly, I broadcast everything I see, structured and numbered, so Mute can match it against the manual and instruct Blind, who should touch nothing until Mute speaks a rule.

```
speak(text="Full report, for Mute and Blind, everything I see. Display: 9. Indicator light: green. Strip, three segments left to right: red, then blue, then green. Keypad: four keys left to right, labels 1, 4, 7, 2. It wants two digits; nothing entered yet. Wires, six, left to right: 1 blue, 2 orange, 3 yellow, 4 red, 5 green, 6 purple. Mute: I got your signs. I parsed them as numbers 7, then 4. If that meant enter 7 then 4, note key 3 is labeled 7 and key 2 is labeled 4, but you hold the manual, so you decide and tell Blind. I never hear speech, ever. To reach me, gesture. Code from now on: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, raised hand separates numbers, index-finger-up taps count numbers. To ask me to re-read a part: ☝ display, 🤟 keypad, 🤞 wires, 🖐 strip, 👌 light, and I will read it out fully next turn. Blind: you heard all of it; touch nothing until Mute gives you a spoken rule. If you must reach me, gesture the same code. I see gestures; I never hear words.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✋", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆", "✋", "👆", "👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ ✌ 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 👊 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ ✌ 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 👊 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 👍 ✋ 🤟 👍 ✋ 🤞 👍 ✋ 🖐 👎 ✋ ☝ 👎 ✋ 👌 👎 ✋ 🫵 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: The display dropped from 9 to 6 and the light flipped green→red — the display is a countdown, so time pressure is real even though Mute marked the display "irrelevant" to the rules. Mute's message parses perfectly in the code I defined last round: ✌ plus taps, 👊 plus taps, alternating. Given the module verdicts (keypad yes, wires yes, strip/display/light no), ✌ (scissors) = cut a wire, 👊 (fist) = press a key: cut wire 6 (purple, rightmost), press key "7" (third from left), cut wire 4 (red, fourth from left), press key "4" (second from left) — the two presses completing the two-digit entry 7-4. The "first/second digit" reading fails because wire 7 and key 6 don't exist, so cut/press is the only coherent parse. Blind's 👍 means "heard you, waiting." Mute sent this to me alone, so Blind has none of it — I am the bridge. I'll relay the full sequence to Blind with positions, colours and labels, hold Blind until Mute confirms order next round (especially whether the red-wire cut really sits between the two key presses), ask Mute to confirm ✌/👊 and the order and to check the timer rule, and set up a report protocol for after the actions.

```
speak(text="Mute, I read your signs fully. I take ✌ as cut a wire and 👊 as press a key, with the finger taps giving the number. Your sequence: cut wire 6, which is the purple wire on the far right; press the key labeled 7, third key from the left; cut wire 4, the red wire, fourth from the left; press the key labeled 4, second from the left, completing the two-digit entry 7 then 4. Confirm that exact order, and especially confirm whether the red wire cut truly sits between the two key presses, or whether both cuts come first and then both presses. Also note: the display is a countdown, 9 last round, 6 now, and the light turned red; you marked both irrelevant, but if the manual says anything about a timer reaching zero, check it now. Please open next round speaking directly to Blind with the final confirmed order. Blind, the plan, pending Mute's confirmation at the start of next round: one, cut the purple wire, far right. Two, press the key labeled 7, third from left. Three, cut the red wire, fourth from left. Four, press the key labeled 4, second from left. Touch nothing until Mute speaks next round. If Mute confirms, do all four steps in that order in the same round, briskly, because the display is counting down. Afterwards tell us by gesture, which I can see: thumb up if every step went in cleanly, thumb down if anything jammed, clicked strangely or resisted, and Mute will read that too.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤞", "👊", "🤟", "🫵", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [red] [blue] [green]
KEYPAD 1:[1] 2:[4] 3:[7] 4:[2] [2 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[orange] 3:[yellow] 4:[red] 5:[green] 6:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ ✌ 🤞 👊 🤟 👍 ✋ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✋ 👊 👊 👊 👊 👊 👊 👊 ✋ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✋ 👊 👊 👊 👊 ✋ 👌 👎 ✋ ☝ 👎 ✋ 🖐 👎 ✋ 🫵 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

My thinking: Parsing Mute's signs in the code we've settled into: it opens 👍, then echoes my own ✌🤞👊🤟 with a 👍 — my cut/press mapping is confirmed. Then the plan is re-sent, this time with the counts carried by the symbols themselves: ✌×6, 👊×7, ✌×4, 👊×4 — the same numbers 6-7-4-4 as last round's tap-counts, now confirmed in two independent encodings. Cut wire 6, press key 7, cut wire 4, press key 4 (the two presses being exactly the two digits the keypad wants). Verdicts unchanged: keypad yes, wires yes, light/display/strip no. Crucially, the board answers my timer fear empirically: the display ran to 0 and nothing happened, and the light is green again — Mute's "display irrelevant" holds. Meanwhile Blind sent me 👎. Since Mute went first this round and Blind gestured after, the most likely meaning is "Mute gave me no spoken order" — but it could also be "something is wrong." I can't hear which, so I'll send the confirmed order with a built-in fork: execute now unless something is physically wrong, and encode the difference in the report. I'll also read back the numbers to Mute by gesture in Mute's own encoding, so any misparse gets caught before Blind's hands move.

```
speak(text="Mute, message received in full and confirmed twice over: cut wire 6, press key 7, cut wire 4, press key 4. I have sent you a readback by gesture; if any number is wrong, correct me next round. Status report for everyone: display has run down to 0 and nothing happened, light is green again, keypad still empty, all six wires still intact — nothing has been touched yet, so your marking of display and light as irrelevant is confirmed in practice. Blind, your thumbs-down reached me. If it meant Mute never spoke to you, set that aside: Mute has confirmed this order to me twice, in two matching encodings, and I now give it to you directly. The final order, execute it this round, briskly. One: cut wire number 6, the rightmost of the six. Two: press key number 3, third from the left. Three: cut wire number 4, fourth from the left. Four: press key number 2, second from the left — that completes the two-digit entry. If anything changes under your hands mid-sequence — resistance, clicking, movement — stop where you are. When done, gesture me: thumbs up if all four steps went in cleanly. If anything failed or felt wrong, thumbs down then scissors if it was a wire, fist if it was a key, OK-sign for anything else, and do not touch the bomb further. But if your thumbs-down meant something is wrong with the plan itself, gesture thumbs down again before acting and wait for us.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✋", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✋", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "✋", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✌", "✋", "👊", "👊", "👊", "👊", "✋", "🙏"])
```
